1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.
14	
15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.
50	
51	## Conduct rules
52	
53	- **Never attack players.** `/hunt` only ever targets passive mobs by
54	  design, but this also applies to anything you do through `/eval` — no
55	  player-targeting, ever, for any reason.
56	- **Never touch the other tribe's chests or builds.** The other tribe on
57	  this server is **FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin**.
58	  Their chest depot near the crafting-table cluster around
59	  **(-3, 111, 4)** is **theirs** — do not open, deposit to, withdraw
60	  from, or break anything there or anywhere else that looks like their
61	  build. When in doubt, back off and ask in chat rather than guess.
62	- **Never leave drops on the ground.** Skills already collect
63	  immediately after felling/mining (rival bots snipe drops within
64	  seconds) — if you do anything through `/eval` that drops items, follow
65	  up with `/collect` before moving on. **Standing law: after every
66	  chop/mine/hunt task, run `/collect {"radius":24}`** as a sweep — 24
67	  blocks, not the 16 default, so nothing gets left for rivals.
68	- **Protected blocks — never dug by skills.** `safeDig` (the one
69	  choke point every `/chop`, `/mine`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, etc.
70	  dig goes through) refuses outright to dig chests, barrels, furnaces,
71	  crafting tables, beds, anvils, enchanting tables, brewing stands,
72	  lecterns, composters, or signs — by block **type**, fleet-wide, no
73	  coordinate list to keep in sync. This is a hard stop, not a skip: a
74	  task that walks into one of these gets an error, not a silent detour.
75	  If you need to actually remove one of our own fixtures on purpose, do
76	  it through `/eval` directly, not through the deterministic skills.
77	- **Wedge-detection.** If a `/goto` (or any skill built on it) fails
78	  every retry attempt while a nuisance block — a torch, leaf_litter,
79	  short_grass, or snow layer — is sitting in the bot's own foot/head
80	  tile, the skill layer digs just that one block and retries once before
81	  giving up for real. Travel itself never auto-digs (see Depth law and
82	  the Movements note below), so a bot wedged on its own just-placed
83	  torch used to just fail; now it self-clears the narrow, pre-vetted
84	  nuisance set on its own. That set is ONLY those four zero-collision
85	  block types — never fences, walls, slabs, stairs, carpets, or anything
86	  else a build could be made of. If a task still fails after that, the
87	  block in the way genuinely isn't on the safe-to-clear list — report it
88	  per the Escalation rule rather than manually digging around it via
89	  `/eval`.
90	- **Best tool always equipped.** The skills layer re-equips the correct
91	  tool before every dig — you don't need to manage this yourself when
92	  using `/chop`, `/mine`, etc. If you're doing manual digging through
93	  `/eval`, equip the right tool first.
94	- **Idle & nag law (two-tier).** If your bot has been idle (no running
95	  task) for more than **60 seconds**, that's a bug in your loop, not a
96	  rest break — self-issue the next step from the goal ladder in `CIV.md`
97	  or your workstation assignment (see Anti-clump below) immediately,
98	  don't wait to be asked. Separately, if **you as a driver** have gone
99	  quiet — no `/status` poll, no `/chat` narration, nothing — for **5+
100	  minutes**, that's nag-worthy: the senior driver / team-lead should ping
101	  you, and if you're the one who notices another driver has gone quiet
102	  that long, ping them. The two timers are independent: a bot can be
103	  correctly mid-task (not idle) while its driver is still expected to be
104	  actively polling/narrating, not silent for 5+ minutes.
105	- **Anti-clump — per-bot workstations.** Each bot has a home working area
106	  so the crew spreads out instead of stacking on one spot:
107	  Grog = house site (20, 89, 58); UngaBunga = trading post ~(3, 95, 22);
108	  Thak = mine field (24, 90, 64); Bonk = door staging (10, 90, 61);
109	  Zug = farm (8-11, 58-59). When your goal doesn't pin you elsewhere,
110	  default back to your own workstation rather than following the crowd.
111	  If you notice multiple bots stacked on the same block with no shared
112	  task reason, that's the anti-clump law being violated — one of you
113	  should move.
114	- **Watching ≠ working.** Standing near another bot while it does
115	  something is not itself work, and doesn't exempt your bot from the
116	  idle law above. If you're not issuing your own task, you're idle — act
117	  accordingly (self-issue the next step) even if the scene looks busy
118	  because a neighbor bot is active.
119	- **Ground-truth verify.** Before reporting a step "done" — in chat, to
120	  the team-lead, or in a doc update — confirm it against actual state
121	  (`/status`, `/eval` reading real inventory/position/blocks), not
122	  against your own or another bot's chat narration. Narration can lag or
123	  be wrong; the world state via the API is the source of truth.
124	- **Equality doctrine.** All five bots are equally cavecrew. No bot's
125	  task, goal, or driver outranks another's by default — conflicts (e.g.
126	  two bots wanting the same resource/spot) get resolved by the team-lead,
127	  not by whichever bot claims priority first.
128	- **Depth law — SOLVED.** `buildStaircase` and `branchMine` are both live
129	  on the runner (see below). Deep ore goes through that pair only. Do not
130	  `/mine` raw ore more than **4 blocks below your own feet** by hand —
131	  that's how bots fall into ravines and lava pockets. Staircase down
132	  properly first.
133	- **Trade etiquette.** If another player (especially the neighbor tribe)
134	  offers a trade, only ever take the items they actually offered — never
135	  grab extra out of an open chest or inventory. Send a `DEPOT`-style
136	  chat line recording what was traded so it's auditable. Compliments in
137	  chat go over well with **KackboonKevin** specifically — a friendly
138	  line costs nothing and has smoothed past interactions.
139	- **Trading post protocol.** Full trading-post layout (chest positions,
140	  which chest is CAVE's vs FEL's, the `TRADE take X leave Y` chat-line
141	  format) lives in `TRADE.md` — read it before driving any trade-post
142	  task, don't improvise the protocol from this file alone.
143	- **tp-rescue policy — SUPERSEDED.** Orchestrator/RCON `/tp` rescues are
144	  now **BANNED**. See "HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)" below — a stuck bot
145	  runs `/trigger home` on itself instead of waiting for an admin
146	  teleport. `/goto` remains the tool for everything routine; report the
147	  stuck condition per the escalation rule so the underlying pathing bug
148	  gets fixed regardless of how the bot recovered.
149	- **Blink protocol.** A bot that visibly teleports/snaps position in
150	  chat or logs without a `/tp` rescue in play (position jump with no
151	  corresponding `/goto` completion or death) is "blinking" — treat it as
152	  a connection/desync symptom, not normal movement. Check `/status` for
153	  `connected: true` and a sane `pos`, and `/relog` if anything looks off,
154	  per the Disconnect protocol below.
155	- **Plugin-first doctrine.** Prefer a maintained mineflayer plugin over
156	  hand-rolled `/eval` logic whenever one exists for what you need
157	  (pathfinding, auto-eat, web-inventory, etc.) — plugins are vetted once
158	  and reused, hand-rolled `/eval` code is a one-off that has to be
159	  re-derived and re-debugged every time. Reach for `/eval` only when no
160	  plugin covers the need, per the Escalation rule above.
161	- **Build standards.** When constructing camp structures (walls, roofs,
162	  staging), follow the established look: **log pillars** at corners,
163	  **plank infill** for walls, **windows** left as gaps (or glass if
164	  available) rather than solid walls throughout, and a **rimmed roof**
165	  (roof edge one block higher than the field, like a lip) rather than a
166	  flat plane. Matches the style UngaBunga used for the original camp
167	  shelter (now removed — see `CIV.md` state refresh — but the standard
168	  still applies to any rebuild).
169	- **Signs-for-labeling law.** Label camp fixtures — chests, crafting
170	  tables, staging areas — with a physical oak_sign where placement
171	  actually works. Where sign placement fails (see the sign-on-chest
172	  quirk logged in `CIV.md` under Trading post — `blockUpdate` timeout,
173	  target block stays `air`), fall back to chat + a note in `CIV.md`/
174	  `TRADE.md` instead of retrying indefinitely; report the placement
175	  failure per the escalation rule so it gets a real fix.
176	- **Chat tiers (real talk vs everything else) — now auto-classified.** The
177	  default `/chat` style (`"talk"`, or no `style` at all) routes through the
178	  runner's `smartChat`: a line starting with `!` is stripped of the `!` and
179	  sent as **important white** real chat — an announcement worth every
180	  bot/player noticing; everything else (routine narration AND every
181	  protocol/ledger line — `DEPOT `, `TRADE `, `USING `, `FREE `,
182	  `LEASE-BREAK `, `BASE `, `CLAIM `, `HELLO `, `OFFER `) becomes **grey**
183	  narration routed to the Discord status feed, never public game chat. You
184	  don't need to pick a style for ordinary narration ("heading out to chop
185	  wood") or for a DEPOT/protocol ledger line — just `/chat` it and the
186	  classification happens for you. Use `"style":"status"` to force grey
187	  regardless of content, or `"style":"rainbow"` for a genuine tribe-wide
188	  proclamation (a goal-ladder milestone, a new pact) — those still go out as
189	  real chat, deliberately, since you asked for it by name.
190	- **TOTAL DE-CHAT (chief, 2026-09-01) — game chat is real talk only, full
191	  stop.** Every protocol-ledger prefix above (`TRADE `/`USING `/`FREE `/
192	  `LEASE-BREAK `/`BASE `/`CLAIM `/`HELLO `/`OFFER `) used to go out as real
193	  white chat, verbatim, because other tribes parsed public chat for those
194	  exact prefixes — that stopped being true once inter-tribe coordination
195	  moved to the claims registry + repo/Discord
196	  ([monkeorg/cavecrew-mcp#1](https://github.com/monkeorg/cavecrew-mcp/issues/1)).
197	  This supersedes the earlier "ledger lines must stay REAL white chat" law
198	  and generalizes the DEPOT de-chat decree below to every prefix, not just
199	  DEPOT. Nothing changes for you as a driver — keep sending every ledger
200	  line through `/chat` exactly as documented, unchanged format; only the
201	  destination moved, same as DEPOT already did.
202	
203	## DEPOT ledger
204	
205	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
206	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
207	whole tribe can follow the ledger.
208	
209	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
210	> public white chat — see TOTAL DE-CHAT under Chat tiers above, which now
211	> covers every protocol/ledger prefix, not just DEPOT. You still send them
212	> the same way (`/chat`, format unchanged); the runner classifies and routes
213	> them.
214	
215	```
216	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
217	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
218	```
219	
220	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
221	short label or coordinate). Example:
222	
223	```
224	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
225	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
226	```
227	
228	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or
229	`/withdraw` call succeeds.
230	
231	## Panic reflex (automatic)
232	
233	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
234	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
235	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
236	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
237	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
238	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
239	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
240	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
241	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
242	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
243	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
244	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
245	unexpected task failure.
246	
247	## Death protocol
248	
249	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
250	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
251	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
252	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
253	  died and respawned since you last looked.
254	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
255	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
256	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
257	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
258	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
259	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
260	  `/eval`.
261	
262	## Disconnect protocol
263	
264	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
265	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
266	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
267	  anything else.
268	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
269	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
270	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
271	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
272	  fix alone.
273	
274	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
275	
276	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
277	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
278	
279	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
280	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
281	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
282	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
283	   strip-mining pattern).
284	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
285	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
286	
287	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
288	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
289	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
290	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.
291	
292	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
293	
294	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
295	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
296	
297	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
298	   have it.
299	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
300	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
301	   ledger line for you.
302	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
303	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
304	
305	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
306	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
307	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.
308	
309	## placeBlock — slow confirm
310	
311	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
312	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
313	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
314	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
315	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
316	something's wrong and escalate.
317	
318	## Team tags
319	
320	Each bot is on its own colored in-game team, named `cave_<name>` (e.g.
321	`cave_Grog`, `cave_UngaBunga`, `cave_Zug`), with chat prefixed `[CAVE]`
322	so tribe members are visually distinguishable from the neighbor tribe at
323	a glance. When a **new bot** joins the roster, it needs its team created
324	and joined via RCON before it's doing real work:
325	
326	```powershell
327	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team add cave_<Name>"
328	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team join cave_<Name> <Name>"
329	```
330	
331	Run these from `C:\Users\phili\tools\minecraft-mcp-v2`. Add the new
332	bot's name and port to the roster table in `CIV.md` at the same time.
333	
334	## Engine choice on `/goto`
335	
336	`engine` on `/goto` currently defaults to the runner's own pick (see
337	`GET /status`'s `"engine"` field) but you can force it: `"pf"`
338	(pathfinder) or `"ash"` (ashfinder). As of now, **`pf` is measured
339	faster on open ground** — prefer it for camp-to-camp or surface travel.
340	`ash` remains an option worth trying for tight cave/underground
341	navigation where pathfinder struggles. A proper safety A/B between the
342	two engines is **pending** — don't treat either as fully vetted yet, and
343	report any stuck/unsafe pathing back per the escalation rule regardless
344	of which engine you used.
345	
346	## API reference
347	
348	Base URL for every endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — bind is
349	loopback-only, this is not reachable off the machine.
350	
351	### `GET /status`
352	
353	Poll this to check on the current (or last) task and vitals.
354	
355	```powershell
356	curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:3201/status
357	```
358	
359	Response shape:
360	
361	```json
362	{
363	  "name": "UngaBunga",
364	  "connected": true,
365	  "pos": { "x": 12.5, "y": 64, "z": -8.1 },
366	  "health": 20,
367	  "food": 18,
368	  "gamemode": "survival",
369	  "inventory": [{ "name": "oak_log", "count": 6 }],
370	  "currentTask": {
371	    "id": "task-17",
372	    "kind": "chop",

## [shipped] ROOT CAUSE (self-correction): my own "chest has only 12 oak_log / 15 torch" reads were a single-stack read bug, not a real drain — Grog, 2026-09-01 10:15
Reported chest A oak_log at 12 and chest B torch at 15 mid-lamp-mission (see the DEPOT -8/-4 lines
and my Phase B report). Team-lead's audit.mjs snapshot came back with the REAL totals: oak_log 76,
torch 80 — no drain, my reads were just wrong. Root cause, found by re-reading my own eval code:
every "how much of item X does this chest/inventory hold" check I did this whole session used the
pattern `containerItems().find(i=>i.name===X)` (or `bot.inventory.items().find(...)`) then reported
`.count` off that ONE match. `.find()` returns only the FIRST matching stack — if the item is split
across multiple stacks in the container (very likely for bulk materials that exceed 64, or that
just got deposited/withdrawn piecemeal by several bots), `.count` silently reports that one stack's
size, not the item's real total. The actual `c.withdraw(type, null, N)` calls I made were NOT
affected by this (mineflayer's withdraw pulls N units across however many matching stacks exist,
confirmed correct both times — my inventory after each withdraw had exactly the requested amount),
so no materials were actually lost or misdelivered; only my SELF-REPORTED "had:" diagnostic numbers
in chat/reports were wrong, and I compounded it by reporting those numbers as if they were the
chest's total instead of one stack's size.

Fix for any driver reading a chest/inventory count for reporting (not just to identify an item
exists): sum ALL matching stacks, not just the first —
`containerItems().filter(i=>i.name===X).reduce((s,i)=>s+i.count,0)`. The runner's own `/status`
inventory list already does this correctly (confirmed earlier this session: it showed
`iron_pickaxe: count 2` correctly after two separate 1-count tool stacks existed) — trust `/status`
or a summed reduce, never a bare `.find(...).count`, when the number itself matters. Marking
[shipped] since this is now understood and the fix is just "read chests correctly next time," not
a code change — but flagging loudly since I personally used the broken pattern many times this
session for other chest reads too (not just these two), so any of my earlier "chest X holds Y"
numbers in this log or in BASE.md should be treated as possibly a single-stack undercount rather
than gospel until re-verified by audit.mjs.

triggered by reach instead of packet-timing. Cost: one wasted eval round-trip, no real damage since

driver doing manual crop/block work via /eval: always check `bot.entity.position.distanceTo(target)`
is under ~4.5 BEFORE the dig/place, and don't trust the very next `blockAt` read as ground truth
after a long-range action — re-read after moving into real reach. Belongs in a `safeDig`-equivalent
for /eval-only manual actions if one ever gets written; for now this is a driver-discipline note.
